situation: You are a member of a student group project, but one teammate has not contributed anything for three weeks and the deadline is close.
tasks: Describe the situation without blaming anyone unfairly.
Explain what the group has already tried.
Ask for advice on how the work will be graded.

situation: You were offered two internships at the same time and need more time to decide on one of them.
to: Ms. Laurent, HR Manager at Brightline
tasks: Thank her for the offer.
Explain why you need more time.
Ask for a specific extension and confirm your interest.

situation: The campus library recently reduced its opening hours, which makes it hard for students who work during the day.
tasks: Explain how the change affects students like you.
Suggest a practical solution.
Offer to help collect student opinions.

situation: You attended a conference talk and want to ask the speaker about her research for your thesis.
tasks: Introduce yourself and mention her talk.
Explain how her research relates to your thesis.
Ask whether she could share an article or meet online.

situation: Your landlord has not repaired the heating in your apartment despite two previous requests, and it is now winter.
tasks: Remind him of your earlier requests.
Explain the consequences of the problem.
State clearly what you expect and by when.

situation: You want to propose a new environmental initiative at your workplace to reduce paper and energy waste.
tasks: Describe the current problem.
Outline two concrete measures.
Explain the benefits for the company.

situation: A classmate copied part of your essay, and the teacher thinks you copied it from him.
tasks: Explain the situation calmly.
Describe evidence that the work is yours.
Ask for a meeting to clarify the issue.

situation: You are organizing an international food evening for exchange students and need the student union's support.
tasks: Describe the event and its purpose.
Explain what support you need.
Explain how the event benefits the student community.

situation: You missed a mid-term exam because of a family emergency and want to take it later.
tasks: Explain what happened and apologize for the late notice.
Mention any documents you can provide.
Ask about the possibility of a make-up exam.

situation: Your company's new scheduling software has caused several mistakes in staff shifts.
tasks: Describe the mistakes with examples.
Explain their impact on your team.
Ask for training or a fix and suggest a timeline.

situation: You read an article in the local newspaper about closing a community sports center, and you disagree.
to: The editor of the City Gazette
tasks: State your opinion clearly.
Give two reasons why the center is important.
Suggest an alternative to closing it.

situation: You want to change from your current degree program to a different one at the same university.
tasks: Explain why you want to change programs.
Ask which of your credits can be transferred.
Request an appointment to discuss your options.

situation: A hotel you booked for a work trip canceled your reservation at the last minute.
tasks: Describe what happened.
Explain the costs and problems this caused you.
Request appropriate compensation.

situation: You would like to become a teaching assistant for an introductory course next semester.
tasks: Explain your interest in the position.
Describe your relevant experience.
Ask about the responsibilities and selection process.

situation: Your team at work needs to choose between two project proposals, and you support one of them.
tasks: Summarize both proposals fairly.
Explain why you prefer one.
Invite comments before the final decision.

situation: The bus route to your university was changed, and students now arrive late to morning classes.
tasks: Explain how the new route affects students.
Provide specific examples of delays.
Suggest a change to the schedule.

situation: You received a scholarship and want to thank the foundation that funds it.
tasks: Express your gratitude.
Explain how the scholarship will help your studies.
Describe your goals for the future.

situation: A colleague often interrupts you in meetings, and it is affecting your work.
tasks: Raise the issue politely and directly.
Give a specific example.
Suggest how you could work better together.

situation: Your research survey needs more participants, and you want students from another department to take part.
to: Dr. Patel, Head of the Psychology Department
tasks: Explain the purpose of your survey.
Describe what participants need to do.
Ask if she can share the survey with her students.

situation: You ordered a laptop for your studies, and it arrived with a damaged screen.
tasks: Give the order details.
Describe the damage and how you discovered it.
Explain which solution you prefer and why.

situation: You were not selected for a job you applied for and want feedback.
tasks: Thank her for the interview.
Ask for specific feedback on your application.
Express interest in future opportunities.

situation: Your university plans to replace printed textbooks with digital ones, and you have concerns.
tasks: State your main concerns.
Explain who might be disadvantaged.
Suggest a compromise.

situation: You want to invite a local business owner to speak at a career event you are organizing.
to: Mr. Bennett, owner of Bennett Design
tasks: Introduce the event and audience.
Explain why you chose him.
Give the practical details and ask for his reply.

situation: You led a volunteer project last month and want to report the results to the organization's director.
to: Ms. Okoro, Director of Green Hands
tasks: Summarize what the volunteers achieved.
Mention one difficulty and how you solved it.
Recommend an improvement for next time.

situation: Your flatmates disagree about how to share the electricity bill.
tasks: Describe the disagreement fairly.
Propose a clear system for sharing the costs.
Ask everyone to confirm by a certain date.

situation: You want to extend your stay in a study-abroad program for another semester.
tasks: Explain why you want to stay longer.
Ask about the requirements and deadlines.
Ask how this affects your visa and housing.

situation: A new rule bans students from eating in the library study rooms, and many students are unhappy.
tasks: Acknowledge the reasons for the rule.
Explain why students are unhappy.
Suggest a balanced alternative.

situation: You have been asked to mentor a new employee, but you are worried about your own workload.
tasks: Express your willingness to help.
Explain your concern about workload.
Propose a way to make it work.

situation: You found an error in the grading of your final exam.
tasks: Identify the question and the error.
Explain why you believe your answer was correct.
Ask politely for the grade to be reviewed.

situation: Your neighborhood has no safe crossing near the primary school, and you want the city to act.
tasks: Describe the danger with examples.
Explain who is affected.
Request a specific action.

situation: You want to start a peer tutoring program in your department.
tasks: Describe how the program would work.
Explain its benefits for students.
Ask for resources and approval.

situation: You took an online course that was very different from its description.
tasks: Explain what the course promised.
Describe how it was different.
Request a refund or another course.

situation: You want to work part-time while studying but are unsure if your visa allows it.
tasks: Explain your situation.
Ask about the rules for working hours.
Ask what documents you need.

situation: Your company is considering a four-day work week and asked employees for their opinion.
tasks: Give your opinion on the proposal.
Explain one advantage and one risk.
Suggest how it could be tested.

situation: A guest lecture was canceled without notice, and many students traveled to campus for nothing.
tasks: Describe what happened.
Explain the inconvenience to students.
Suggest how communication could be improved.

situation: You want to apply for a research grant and need a letter of recommendation.
tasks: Describe the grant and your project.
Explain why you are asking her.
Provide the deadline and offer any information she needs.

situation: Your gym changed its membership fees without informing members in advance.
tasks: Explain the change you noticed.
Say why this is unfair.
Ask what options you have.

situation: You are planning a field trip for your class and need permission to use the university minibus.
tasks: Explain the purpose of the trip.
Give the date, route and number of students.
Ask about the booking procedure.

situation: You want to give feedback on a course that you found useful but too fast.
tasks: Say what you found valuable.
Explain the problem with the pace.
Suggest a specific improvement.

situation: A friend has asked you to help him choose a university abroad.
tasks: Ask about his priorities.
Suggest two factors he should consider.
Offer to share your own experience.

situation: Your workplace has no quiet area for focused work, and noise is affecting productivity.
tasks: Describe the problem.
Explain its effect on your work.
Propose a practical solution.

situation: You want to publish an article in the student magazine about mental health on campus.
tasks: Describe your article idea.
Explain why the topic matters now.
Ask about length and deadlines.

situation: A delivery company left your package outside in the rain, and the contents were damaged.
tasks: Describe what happened.
Explain the damage.
Request compensation and better procedures.

situation: You have been asked to give a presentation at short notice and need more preparation time.
tasks: Acknowledge the request.
Explain why more time would improve the result.
Propose a new date.

situation: Your local council wants to build a shopping center on a popular green space.
tasks: State your position.
Explain the value of the green space.
Suggest an alternative location or plan.

situation: You and a classmate want to start a podcast about science for the university radio.
tasks: Describe the podcast concept.
Explain what makes it interesting for listeners.
Ask about equipment and broadcast times.

situation: You want to request flexible working hours to attend evening classes.
tasks: Explain why you are taking the classes.
Propose a new schedule.
Show how your work will not suffer.

situation: Your university's online learning platform crashes often during exam periods.
tasks: Describe the problem and when it happens.
Explain the consequences for students.
Suggest how to prevent it.

situation: A former classmate asked you to recommend her for a job at your company.
tasks: Respond to her request.
Explain what the job involves.
Give advice on how to prepare her application.

situation: You want to organize a charity run to raise money for the local hospital.
tasks: Describe your plan.
Explain how the money will be collected.
Ask how the hospital can support the event.
